title: Module 4: The AEGISAXIOM Ecosystem & Digital Workforce
description: Tests fluency with the 6 AEGISAXIOM AI agents (Orion, Pulsar, Zenith, Lyra, Vega, Callisto), the 3 AI archetypes (Automated Workflows, Conversational AIs, Web Apps), AEGISAXIOM as central orchestrator, and dashboard literacy.
instructions: Answer all questions to the best of your ability. You cannot ask ARC for help while the quiz is in progress. Aim for 10-12 minutes.

questions.prompt: A prospect's CFO asks: 'Of all the AEGISAXIOM agents, which one would actually write our Statements of Work after a discovery call?' Which agent should you name?
questions.explanation: Orion is the SOW Builder. It takes the structured intelligence from a completed discovery process (specifically, the AI Employee Matrix that Vega produces after Call 3) and drafts the full SOW — executive summary, scope of work, milestones, financial justification, assumptions and risks. Vega does the discovery and analysis upstream of Orion, but Vega hands off to Orion — it doesn't write the SOW itself.

questions.prompt: Match each client need to the AEGISAXIOM agent that solves it.

items.label: We need to evaluate thousands of policy rules in milliseconds every time a transaction comes in
We need an AI that listens to our sales calls and surfaces what we missed asking
We need real-time analytics dashboards that pull from our entire AEGISAXIOM workspace
We need automated communication — emails, Slack messages, follow-ups — triggered by workflow events

questions.explanation: Pulsar is the rules engine — high-throughput policy evaluation. Vega is the research/discovery agent that analyzes call transcripts and identifies gaps. Zenith is the analytics layer. Lyra handles outbound communication. Memorize these mappings — you will be asked them on every Call 1, and getting them wrong costs you credibility on the spot.

questions.prompt: A client asks: 'What's the difference between an Automated Workflow and a Conversational AI in AEGISAXIOM?' Which is the most accurate answer?

options.label: Automated Workflows are deterministic event-triggered pipelines (often built with LangChain). Conversational AIs are dialog-based agents that hold multi-turn conversations and call tools dynamically.
Automated Workflows use Python and Conversational AIs use JavaScript
Automated Workflows are for finance and Conversational AIs are for customer service
There's no real difference — they're just two names for the same thing

questions.explanation: A is correct. The defining distinction is execution model: Automated Workflows are triggered by an event (a webhook fires, a row gets inserted, a schedule hits) and run a deterministic chain of steps. Conversational AIs run as long as a human is talking to them, dynamically selecting tools and keeping state across turns. Both archetypes coexist in AEGISAXIOM, plus a third (Web Apps for human-facing interfaces).

questions.prompt: True or False: AEGISAXIOM itself is a passive container — the individual agents (Orion, Pulsar, Zenith, etc.) operate independently and don't share a central orchestration layer.
questions.explanation: False. AEGISAXIOM is the central interface and orchestrator — agents share state, route work to each other, inherit governance from the platform layer, and surface their results through unified dashboards. The whole point is that you don't manage 6 disconnected tools; you manage one platform that contains 6 specialized roles. Selling AEGISAXIOM as 'a bundle of separate agents' undersells the architecture by a wide margin.

questions.prompt: A skeptical prospect points at the AEGISAXIOM dashboard and says: 'Orion has 94% accuracy and 4.2 minute average completion. Why should I care about those numbers?' What's the strongest answer?

options.label: 94% means almost no errors, and 4.2 minutes means it's fast

Those metrics are how you forecast ROI: 94% accuracy means human review is the exception not the rule (so labor savings are real), and 4.2 minutes vs the 4-hour human baseline tells you the velocity gain (~57x) you can plug into your MMI calculation
Those are vanity metrics — the real number is the cost per execution
94% is industry-leading and proves AEGISAXIOM is better than every competitor

questions.explanation: B is the right framing. Dashboard literacy is what separates a rep who reads numbers from a rep who CONVERTS numbers into a forecast. Accuracy ≥ 90% means review-by-exception (you can credit the labor savings honestly). Velocity gains (the ratio of human time to agent time) plug straight into the MMI Time dimension you'll use in Module 6. A is technically true but flat. C dismisses the numbers. D is salesy and doesn't actually answer the question.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are TRUE about Callisto, the support agent in the AEGISAXIOM ecosystem? Select all that apply.

options.label: Callisto handles internal user support — answering questions about how to use AEGISAXIOM, surfacing documentation, escalating to humans when needed
Callisto is a Conversational AI archetype, not an Automated Workflow
Callisto writes the Statements of Work after discovery is complete
Callisto runs continuously and is one of the 9 of 11 currently active employees in the AEGISAXIOM workspace

questions.explanation: A, B, and D are correct. C is wrong — that's Orion. Callisto is a Conversational AI focused on internal support and lives alongside the other active agents. The 'active 9 of 11' framing is a useful demo signal: AEGISAXIOM isn't a future promise, it's a workforce that's already running.

questions.prompt: In one or two sentences, why does AEGISAXIOM need a 'Web App' archetype when Automated Workflows and Conversational AIs already exist?
questions.rubric: A passing answer captures the core idea: some tasks need structured human input (approving an expense, filling a form) where chat is too ambiguous and an automated workflow has no human in the loop — Web Apps fill that gap. Either the 'structured input' or 'human-in-the-loop interface' framing earns full credit. Reward concrete examples. Penalize answers that just say 'because UIs are nice.'
